title: Safe Database Migrations in CI/CD
description: Ship schema changes that are backward compatible so app and database versions can coexist during a rolling deploy.

data.text: Your pipeline runs `dotnet ef database update` against Azure SQL immediately before deploying the new app version. Last release it dropped a column the previous app version was still reading, and users saw errors for the four minutes the old instances remained in the load balancer. Fix this.

Adopt **expand/contract** migrations. Every release is backward compatible with the previous app version: release N only **adds** things (new nullable columns, new tables, backfill jobs). Destructive steps such as dropping a column move to release N+1, after no running instance references it. Migrations should be **idempotent and re-runnable**, and they must not hold long locks on large tables.

data.title: Expand/contract across two releases (SQL)
Idempotent migration step in a pipeline
data.code:
- task: SqlAzureDacpacDeployment@1
  displayName: Apply migrations
  inputs:
    azureSubscription: quotient-prod-connection
    ServerName: $(sqlServer).database.windows.net
    DatabaseName: $(sqlDatabase)
    AuthenticationType: servicePrincipal
    deployType: SqlTask
    SqlFile: $(Pipeline.Workspace)/drop/migrations/*.sql
    # every script starts with: IF NOT EXISTS (...) guards

- task: AzureWebApp@1
  displayName: Deploy app (slot swap)
  inputs:
    azureSubscription: quotient-prod-connection
    appName: $(appName)
    deployToSlotOrASE: true
    resourceGroupName: $(resourceGroup)
    slotName: staging

data.text: During any rolling or slot-swap deployment, the old and new app versions run **at the same time** against one database. Any schema change that removes or renames something visible to the old version causes errors during that window, regardless of how fast the deployment is. Expand/contract removes the window entirely.

cards.title: Expand/contract (two releases)
pros: Works with slot swaps and canary
cons: Requires two releases per destructive change
Needs discipline to finish the contract step
